info.title: AlianHub API
info.description: Paths, methods, auth and tags only. The full reference is docs/API.md. Generated by npm run api:doc; do not edit by hand.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Who a token is, and what that person may do.

tags.name: Read-only token API
tags.description: Three reads under `/api/public-v1` that accept an API token and nothing else. They are the simplest way to list projects and tasks. Every read is narrowed to what the token's person can open in the web app, and a token limited to projects reads only those.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Creating a task and changing one. Both routes take the bodies the web app sends, so their field names follow the stored task. To read tasks, use [Everything](#everything) or the [Read-only token API](#read-only-token-api).

tags.name: Everything
tags.description: One list of tasks across every project the caller can read, with filters, grouping, sorting and a cursor, and the caller's saved views of that list.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Duplicating a project, and saving a project as a template to start others from. To list projects, use `GET /api/public-v1/projects`.

tags.name: Pages
tags.description: Docs and wiki pages, their version history, and who a comment on one can name. A page belongs to a project or to the workspace. A private page is its author's alone; any other page is open to whoever can see its project. A page the caller cannot see answers the same as one that does not exist.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Read-only views of the workspace's AI agents: who they are, what they are running and what they have proposed. Runs and proposals are narrowed to the projects and tasks the caller can read.

tags.name: Dashboards
tags.description: The answers of the Ask cards on a dashboard. These two routes sit under `/api/v1`; they are described here because a token can call them.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Managing the webhooks described under [Webhook deliveries](#webhook-deliveries) above. A webhook belongs to the person who created it: nobody else can list, change or delete it, or read its delivery log.

tags.name: Goals
tags.description: Goals with targets that show how far a team or a person has got. A goal has an owner, a period and up to 20 targets; its progress is the weighted average of its targets. A target is a `number`, a `currency` amount, a `boolean` or a `tasks` target counted from lists and tasks. A goal is `private` (its owner), `people` (its owner and the people it is shared with) or `workspace` (every member; a guest only when named). Guests can read goals shared with them and cannot create one. A token limited to projects cannot use these routes. A write made with an agent's token follows the rules that hold that agent.

tags.name: Whiteboards
tags.description: One whiteboard for each list: task cards, sticky notes and text laid out on a canvas. A board is as open as its list: it can be read by whoever can open the list, and changed by whoever can edit the project while the list, its folders and the project are active. The title of a task card is shown only to someone who may open that task.

tags.name: Imports
tags.description: Undoing an import that created tasks in bulk.

tags.name: Custom fields
tags.description: Reading the tasks a relationship field links and the votes on a voting field, and casting a vote.

get.summary: Returns the person and the workspace behind the token, with that person's role and permissions.
Needs a project the caller can open. Answers with `data`: `rules` (`entries` of person and sentence, `fallbackUserId`, `mode`, `onCreate`, `onChange`) and `ai.state`, whether AI is available.

put.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's details. Reads `entries` (a list of at most 50 objects with `userId` and `when`, a sentence of at most 300 characters, one per person), `fallbackUserId` (id or empty), `mode` (`suggest` or `apply`, `suggest` when left out), `onCreate` (boolean, true when left out) and `onChange` (boolean, false when left out) from the body; each person must hold a seat and be able to open the project. Answers with `data`: the saved rules.

post.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's details, and AI must be on with a model configured (409 otherwise). Reads `userIds` (a list of 1 to 10 ids) from the body. Answers with `data.drafts`: a suggested rule sentence for each person who can open the project, based on their recent tasks there.

get.summary: Needs a task the caller can open (404 otherwise). Answers with `data`: `decision`, the latest open suggestion for the task or `null`, and `pending`, whether one is still being worked out.

post.summary: Needs the permission to change a task's assignee in the task's project. Assigns the suggested person to the task; 409 when the suggestion was already handled, the task already has an assignee, or the person can no longer open it. Answers with `data`: the decision.
Needs the permission to change a task's assignee in the task's project. Marks the suggestion dismissed. Answers with `data`: the decision.
Needs the permission to change a task's assignee in the task's project. Takes back an accepted suggestion. Answers with `data`: the decision.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace, and only for a job that person started; any other id answers 404 `Job not found.`. Answers with `data`: the job and its progress.

post.summary: Needs the permission to change a task's custom field. Reads `taskIds` (a list of 1 to 200 ids) and `scope` (`sprint` or left out) from the body; only tasks the caller can open are computed. Answers with `data`: `updated`, the computed `values` and `errors`.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `projectId` (id) and `taskId` (id, used only when the caller can open the task) from the query. Answers with `data`: `names` a formula may use, with the task's values when a task is named, and the lists of `functions` and `rollupFunctions`.

post.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `expression` (string, required), `fieldId`, `fieldTitle`, `projectId` (ids and string) and `sample` (an object of values to try it on) from the body. A formula that does not parse or that closes a cycle answers a failed status with a `code`. Answers with `data`: `references`, `functions`, `preview` and `previewError`.
Returns, for each task named, the tasks its relationship fields link and the tally of its voting fields.

Any signed-in member of the workspace who can edit that field on the task. Reads `proposalIds` (a list of up to 5 ids from a preview the same person made) from the body; an expired one is refused. Answers with `data`: `applied` (task ids) and `refused` (with a reason each).

Any signed-in member of the workspace who can edit that field on the tasks. Reads `taskIds` (a list of ids, up to the workspace's bulk limit) and `proposalIds` (a list of up to 5 ids) from the body. The fill runs in the background. Answers with `data`: the job.

Any signed-in member of the workspace who can edit that field on the task; a task they cannot edit it on comes back with a `reason` instead. Reads `taskIds` (a list of 1 to 5 ids) from the body. Nothing is written. Answers with `data.proposals`: for each task, a `proposalId`, the proposed `text` and `fieldValue`.

Needs the same rights as the usage read; a connected agent is refused. Takes the field and every value of it away for good; archiving (the field update with `isDelete`) hides a field and keeps its values. A field that a rollup or a formula reads answers 409 with the code `FIELD_IS_READ` and the same `readBy` and `readElsewhere`. Answers with `data.tasks`: how many tasks the caller could open held a value.

get.summary: Needs the permission to edit custom fields in the field's projects, and the field setting for a field of every project. Answers with `data`: `tasks` (how many tasks the caller can open hold a value), `partial` (true when the caller cannot open every task), `readBy` (the titles of the rollups and formulas that read this field) and `readElsewhere` (true when a field of a project the caller cannot open reads it). An unknown id answers 404.

post.summary: Casts or withdraws the caller's own vote on a voting field of a task.

Deletes a manual time entry. Needs a task the caller can open. Reads `timeSheetId`, `logTimeDate`, `dateFormat`, `startLogTime`, `endLogTime`, `projectId`, `ticketId`, `sprintId`, `taskName` and `projectName` from the body, all required, plus `timeDuration` (minutes), `userId` and `folderId`. Deleting another person's entry needs the Everyone grant on the user timesheet and an open project, else 403. An entry in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText` `Logtime deleted successfully`. It also writes task history and a notification.

get.summary: Needs a project the caller can open, named by the query field `projectId` (id). Answers with `data`: the project's epics, oldest first, with `taskCount` and `completedCount` counted over the tasks the caller can open.

post.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the project named by `projectId`. Reads `name` (string, required), `projectId` (id, required), `description`, `color`, `priority`, `ownerUserId` (strings), `startDate` and `dueDate` from the body; a failed check answers a failed status with the reason. Answers with `data`: the new epic.

Needs the permission to create tasks in the projects of both the task and the epic. Reads `taskId` (id) and `epicId` (id, or empty or null to take the task out) from the body; a task the caller cannot open, or an epic that does not exist, answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: `taskId` and `epicId`.

put.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the epic's project. Reads `name`, `color`, `description`, `status`, `priority`, `ownerUserId`, `startDate` and `dueDate` from the body and changes the ones sent; a body with none of them answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: the epic as it is now.

delete.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the epic's project. The epic is marked deleted and its tasks are unlinked from it. Answers with `statusText` `Epic deleted.` and no `data`.

post.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the epic's project. Counts the epic's tasks again and answers with `data`: the epic with `taskCount` and `completedCount`, counted for tasks the caller can open.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, and it lists only the caller's own exports (a `uid` of someone else answers 403). Answers with `data`: up to 20 exports, newest first, each with `type`, `format`, `status`, `fileName`, `total`, `processed`, `error` and `createdAt`.

post.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can list the project's tasks (404 otherwise). Reads `format` (`csv` or `xlsx`), `projectId` (id), `sprintId` (id, optional) and `projectName` (string) from the body. The export runs in the background. Answers with `data`: the job.

Owners and admins only. Reads `format` (`csv` or `xlsx`, `xlsx` when left out) from the body. The export runs in the background. Answers with `data`: the job's `_id`, `type`, `format`, `status`, `fileName` and `createdAt`.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it, for an export the caller started; a workspace export also needs the owner or admin role. Answers with the file once the export has finished, and 404 `Export not ready.` before that.

Needs a project the caller can open, named by the query field `projectId` (id); otherwise 404. Answers with `data`: the project's forms, newest first, each with `title`, `description`, `sprintId`, `state` and `submissionCount`.

post.summary: Needs edit rights on the project named in the body (403 without them, 404 when it cannot be seen). Reads `title` (string, required), `projectId` (id, required), `description` (string) and `sprintId` (id) from the body. The form starts as a draft with no questions. Answers with `data`: the form.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Answers with `data`: the questions a form can ask, as `groups`, the `widgets`, `spans`, `gridColumns` and the task fields a question can be mapped to.
Needs a project the caller can open; otherwise 404 `Form not found.`. Answers with `data`: the form with its questions, and its public `url` while it is live.

put.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project. Reads `title`, `description`, `successMessage` (strings), `sprintId` (id), `questions` (list), `defaults` (object) and `state` from the body and changes the ones sent; a failed check answers a failed status with the reason. Answers with `data`: the form as it is now.

delete.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project. A form that is published answers a failed status, and must be taken offline first. The form is marked deleted and the tasks it filed are kept. Answers with `statusText` `Form deleted.` and no `data`.

post.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project (403 without them, 404 when the project cannot be seen). Reads `publish` (boolean, true when left out; false takes the form offline) from the body. A form that fails the checks for going live answers a failed status with the reason. Answers with `data`: `state` and, when live, `token` and `url`.

get.summary: Needs edit rights on the form's project, because submissions hold the submitters' answers. Reads `q` (string, up to 120 characters, matched against every answer), `page` and `limit` (numbers, 10 per page by default and at most 100) and `all` (`1` returns up to 5000 rows for an export) from the query. Answers with `data`: `submissions`, `total`, `page`, `pages` and `truncated`.

Adds a target to a goal and answers with the whole goal.

delete.summary: Removes a target and answers with the whole goal.

Adds a manual time entry to a task, or edits one. Needs a task the caller can open. Reads `logTimeDate`, `description`, `startLogTime`, `endLogTime`, `timeDuration` (a string like `HH:MM`), `ticketId`, `projectId`, `isEdit` (a boolean), `dateFormat`, `taskName`, `projectName`, `sprintId` and `timeZone` from the body, all required, plus `timeSheetId` and `previousLoggedTime` when `isEdit` is true. Optional: `userId`, `billable`, `folderId`, `companyOwnerId`. Logging for another person needs the Everyone grant on the user timesheet and the project must be open to the caller, else 403. The person must be a member (400). An entry in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText` `Logtime added successfully` and `data`: the saved entry. It also writes task history and a notification.

get.summary: Lists pages, without their bodies.

post.summary: Creates a page in a project, or in the workspace when no project is named.

Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `action`, `title`, `instruction` and `currentText` (strings) and `pageId` (id of a page the caller may read, whose title and text fill in what is left out) from the body. Answers with `data`: the composed text, or a failed status with the reason, and `isNotAi` when no AI is set up.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Answers with `data.configured`: whether an AI provider is set up for writing pages.
Returns one page with its body.

put.summary: Changes a page's title, body or properties. Only the keys sent are changed.

delete.summary: Moves a page to the trash, together with the pages under it that the caller can see.

put.summary: Needs edit rights on the page, and a share by name as editor is not enough; a person must make the call. Only a page an agent drafted can be approved, else a failed status. Answers with `data`: the page.

get.summary: Any signed-in member who may read the page. Answers with `data`: the page's comments, oldest first, up to 500, with `limit` and `atLimit`.

post.summary: Any signed-in member who may read the page. Reads `message` (string), `blockId` (string), `parentId` (id of a comment to reply under) and an attached file as `mediaURL`, `mediaOriginalName` and `mediaSize` from the body. A page holds at most 500 comments (409). Answers with `data`: the comment.

get.summary: Lists the ids of the people a comment on a page may mention or be assigned to.

put.summary: Only the comment's author, who must be able to read the page (403 for anyone else). Reads `message` (string) from the body. Answers with `data`: the comment as it is now.

delete.summary: The comment's author or an admin, who must be able to read the page. A thread is deleted with its replies. Answers with `data._id`: the id of the comment.

put.summary: Assigns a comment thread to a person, or clears the assignment.
Puts the caller's reaction on a comment, or takes it off if it is already there.

Any signed-in member who may read the page; a thread that has an assignee can be resolved only by the assignee, the person who assigned it or an admin, and a reply cannot be resolved (400). Reads `resolved` (boolean, true when left out; false reopens the thread) from the body. Answers with `data`: the comment.

post.summary: Needs edit rights on the page. Takes a multipart body with the image as `file`. Answers with `data.key`: the key to put in the page's image block.

put.summary: Takes a page back out of the trash. Only the page itself: the pages that went with it are restored one by one.

Needs edit rights on the page, and a share by name as editor is not enough. Reads `nextReviewDate` (a date, three months ahead when left out) from the body, marks the page as a wiki page reviewed now by the caller, and answers with `data`: the page.

get.summary: Only the page's author, or an owner or admin who can open it (403 for anyone else). Answers with `data`: `people`, each with `userId`, `role`, `by`, `at` and `active`, and `limit`.

put.summary: Only the page's author, or an owner or admin who can open it. Reads `role` (`viewer` or `editor`, `viewer` when left out) from the body; the person must be an active member of the workspace, and a page can be shared with a limited number of people (400 otherwise). Answers with `data`: the list of people the page is shared with.

delete.summary: Only the page's author, or an owner or admin who can open it. Answers with `data`: the list of people the page is still shared with.

get.summary: Lists the versions kept for a page, newest first, without their bodies.

post.summary: Keeps the page as it is now as a version, with a name when one is given.

get.summary: Returns one version with its body.

put.summary: Names a version, or clears its name.

post.summary: Puts a version's title and body back on the page. The page as it was is kept as a version first.

get.summary: Lists the project templates the caller may use, by name.

patch.summary: Changes a template's name, description or whether it is offered to everyone.

delete.summary: Deletes a template and the task rows it kept. Projects made from it are not affected.

post.summary: Creates a project from a template, with its folders, lists and, when asked, its tasks.
Copies a project: its settings, folders, lists and automations, and its tasks when asked.

get.summary: Reports how far the tasks of a large copy have got.

post.summary: Saves a project's settings, folders, lists and, when asked, its tasks and automations as a template.

get.summary: Lists the public links of something.

post.summary: Creates a public link to a list, a report or a page.

put.summary: Switches a public link on or off.

delete.summary: Revokes a public link.

post.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace who can read the target. Reads `targetType` (`task` or `comment`), `targetId` (id), `emoji` (string) and `isProjectComment` (boolean) from the body; the caller's own reaction is added, or removed if it is already there. A target the caller cannot read answers 404. Answers with `data.reactions`: the target's reactions.

Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `query` (string) from the body and matches it against task names and keys, project names, comment text and page titles, within the projects, lists and pages the caller can open. Answers with `data`: `tasks`, `projects`, `comments` and `pages`, each limited in number.
Needs a project the caller can open. Reads `projectId` (id) from the body. Answers with `data`: the project's backlog list, which is made first if it does not exist.

Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the body. Answers with `data`: the sprint's name, state, goal and dates, its totals of tasks, estimate and points, and a `days` series with the ideal line.

Needs write access to the list's project and the permission to create lists there; a person must make the call. Reads `sprintId` (id) and `incompleteDestination` (`next`, `backlog` or the id of an open sprint of the same project, `next` when left out) from the body. Unfinished tasks move to the destination. Answers with `data`: the completed sprint; a sprint already completed answers success and moves nothing.

get.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the query; a list that is not a sprint answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: the sprint's state, commitment, tasks added after the start, and the counts of finished work and of unfinished work with a `list` of it.

post.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the body. Answers with `data`: `plannedMinutes`, `loggedMinutes` and `overdueMinutes`, the minutes the sprint is projected to run over its plan.

get.summary: Needs a project the caller can open and a list the caller can see. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the query; a list that is not a sprint answers a failed status. Answers with `data`: the sprint's state, goal and dates, and the totals of what was committed, completed and left unfinished, with the tasks added after the start and those moved out.

post.summary: Needs write access to the list's project and the permission to create lists there; a person must make the call. Reads `sprintId` (id), `isScrum` (boolean; false turns Scrum off), `goal` (string), `startDate` and `endDate` (dates, both or neither, the end after the start) from the body. A completed sprint cannot be edited, and a running one cannot have Scrum turned off. Answers with `data`: the sprint.

Needs write access to the list's project and the permission to create lists there; a person must make the call. Reads `sprintId` (id) from the body. The list must be a sprint with a start and end date, and a project runs one sprint at a time; the tasks in it become the sprint's commitment. Answers with `data`: the started sprint, or a failed status with the reason.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `projectId` (id, optional) from the query: with it, the workspace's templates and that project's, for a project the caller can open; without it, the workspace's templates and those of every project the caller can open. Answers with `data`, sorted by name, each with `name`, `scope`, `projectId`, `isDefault`, `canManage` and a count of what it carries.

post.summary: Allowed for owners and admins when `scope` is `workspace`, and otherwise for those who can create tasks in the task's project. Reads `name` (string, required), `scope` (`project` or `workspace`, `project` when left out), `taskId` (id of the task to copy from, required) and `include` (an object of booleans, where `false` leaves a part out) from the body. Answers with `data`: the template.

put.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's details. Reads `projectId` (id, required) and `templateId` (id, or empty to clear the default) from the body; the template must be a workspace one or that project's. Answers with `statusText` saying whether a default was set or cleared.

patch.summary: Allowed for owners and admins on a workspace template, and for those who can create tasks in the project on a project template. Reads `name` (string, required) from the body. Answers with `statusText` `Template renamed.` and no `data`.

delete.summary: Allowed for owners and admins on a workspace template, and for those who can create tasks in the project on a project template. The template is marked deleted and is no longer any project's default. Answers with `statusText` `Template deleted.` and no `data`.

post.summary: Needs the permission to create tasks in the task's project; fields the caller's role may not change are skipped and named. Reads `taskId` (id, required), `overwrite` and `preview` (booleans) from the body; with `preview` true nothing is written. Answers with `data`: `applied`, `conflicts`, `skipped`, `checklistAdded` and `subtasksCreated`.
Creates a task, or a subtask when `data.ParentTaskId` names a parent.

patch.summary: Changes one task. `action` names the change, and the other keys of the body depend on it.

post.summary: Runs one change on many tasks at once. The caller must be able to open every task in `taskIds` and hold the permission for the chosen action in their projects, for example `task.task_status` for `bulkUpdateStatus`, `task.task_delete` for `bulkDelete`, `task.task_archive` for `bulkArchive`, `task.task_move` for `bulkMove`. Reads `action` (string, must start with `bulk` and be a known bulk action such as `bulkUpdateStatus`, `bulkUpdatePriority`, `bulkUpdateDueDate`, `bulkUpdateStartDate`, `bulkUpdateDates`, `bulkUpdateAssignee`, `bulkUpdateTags`, `bulkArchive`, `bulkRestore`, `bulkDelete`, `bulkTrash`, `bulkMove`, `bulkConvertToSubTask`, `bulkConvertToTask`, `bulkAddToList`, `bulkDuplicate`) and `taskIds` (list of ids) from the body, plus the fields that action takes, such as `newStatus`, `firebaseObj`, `DueDate`, `startDate`, `employeeId`, `tagId`, `sprintObj`, `projectData`, `parentTaskId`. Answers with `data`: `updated`, `skipped` (task id and reason), `errors`, `totals` (counts of each), and statusText 'Bulk operation completed'. A bad or unknown action answers `status` false with 'Invalid bulk action' or 'Unknown bulk action'. A task or destination the caller cannot open answers 404, a missing permission answers 403.
Lists tasks from every project the caller can read, filtered, grouped, sorted and paged.

get.summary: Lists the caller's own saved views of the Everything list, by name.

post.summary: Saves a view: a name and the settings of the Everything list.

patch.summary: Changes the name, the settings or the default mark of one of the caller's views.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the caller's views.

post.summary: Links two tasks, unlinks them, or lists a task's links. The caller must be able to open the task, with the `task.task_list` permission in its project. Reads `action` (string: `add`, `remove`, `list` or `openBlockers`) and `companyId` from the body, then `taskId` (id, required), and for `add` and `remove` also `relatedTaskId` (id); for `add` it also reads `type` (one of `blocks`, `blocked_by`, `duplicates`, `duplicated_by`, `relates_to`). Answers with the handler's own envelope: `status`, `statusText` and `data`. For `add` and `remove`, `data` holds `taskId`, `relatedTaskId` and `relations` (only the links the caller can open). For `list`, `data` is the linked tasks, each with `taskId`, `type`, `label`, `createdBy`, `createdAt` and a short `task` summary. For `openBlockers`, `data` is the `blocked_by` links whose blocking task is still open. Failures such as a missing task or two tasks already linked answer `status` false with the error text as statusText. An unknown `action` answers `status` false with 'Invalid relation action'.

get.summary: Lists the other lists a task has been added to, besides its own.

post.summary: Approves or rejects several submitted timesheet periods at once. Only an owner or admin has any effect; for others every id is skipped as `not_allowed`. Reads `ids` (a list of record ids, 1 to 100) and `action` (`approve` or `reject`) from the body, both required, plus `reason` (required to reject). Bad input answers 400. Answers with `data`: `results` (one `id` and `outcome` each, `skipped` ones with a `reason`) and `counts` (`approved`, `sent_back`, `skipped`).

get.summary: Lists a person's timesheet submissions, newest period first. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `userId` from the query. Only an owner or admin may read another person's list; for anyone else `userId` is ignored and their own is read. Answers with `data`: the approval records.

Lists submitted timesheet periods that wait for review. Only an owner or admin may call it; others get `status` false with `statusText` `Only an owner or admin can review timesheets.` Reads nothing. Answers with `data`: the submitted records, oldest first.

Lists submitted timesheet periods with the context a reviewer needs. Only an owner or admin may call it; others get `status` false. Reads `hoursPerDay` (a number, default 8) from the query. Answers with `data`: the submitted records, oldest first, each with `userName`, `userAvatar`, `totalMinutes`, `entryCount`, `billableMinutes`, `nonBillableMinutes`, `capacityMinutes` and `overMinutes`.

Reads the approval record of one timesheet period. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `periodStart` and `periodEnd` (dates, required) and `userId` from the query. Only an owner or admin may read another person's record; for anyone else `userId` is ignored and their own is read. Answers with `data`: the approval record, or null when none exists.

post.summary: Sends a timesheet period in for approval. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. A member submits their own sheet; an owner or admin may pass another member's `userId`, otherwise it is refused. Reads `periodStart` and `periodEnd` (dates, required), `periodType` (string, default `week`), `note` (string) and `userId` from the body. A period that is already approved is refused. It saves the period as submitted with the minutes and entry count logged in it. Answers with `statusText` `Timesheet submitted for approval.` and `data`: the approval record.

Approves, rejects or reopens a submitted timesheet period. Only an owner or admin may call it; others get `status` false. Reads `id` (the approval record id) from the path and `action` (`approve`, `reject` or `reopen`) and `reason` (string, needed to reject) from the body. The record must be in a state that allows the action. An owner or admin may approve their own week, and the record is marked as self approved. Answers with `statusText` like `Timesheet approved.` and `data`: the updated record.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `kind` (`projects`, `folders`, `lists`, `tasks` or `docs`, `projects` when left out) from the query. Lists only what the caller could open. Answers with `data`: the trashed items, each with a `title`, a `code` and a `projectId`.

put.summary: Needs what deleting that kind needed, in the project the item belongs to; a person must make the call; a doc is judged by the doc rules. The path `kind` is `projects`, `folders`, `lists`, `tasks` or `docs`, and `id` an id. Projects and lists come back together with their tasks. Answers with `data`: the `kind` and `id`.

get.summary: Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Answers with `data`, sorted by name, each template with `name`, `viewType` and `canManage`, which is true for owners and admins.

post.summary: Needs the permission to change the project's views. Reads `projectId` (id), `viewId` (string) and `name` (string) from the body, and keeps the setup of that view as a template; a workspace holds a limited number. Answers with `data`: the template.

patch.summary: Owners and admins only. Reads `name` (string, required) from the body. Answers with `data`: the renamed template.

delete.summary: Owners and admins only. The template is marked deleted. Answers with `statusText` `Template deleted.` and no `data`.

get.summary: Lists the caller's own webhooks. The signing secret is never returned here.

post.summary: Creates a webhook and returns its signing secret, once.

get.summary: Lists the events a webhook can subscribe to.

put.summary: Changes a webhook, or switches it on or off. Only the keys sent are changed.

delete.summary: Deletes a webhook, its delivery log and its signing secret.

get.summary: Lists a webhook's deliveries, newest first.
Returns the board of a list: its cards, notes and texts.

patch.summary: Adds, moves and removes elements on a board, as a change on the revision the caller last read.

get.summary: Lists the earlier states kept for a board, newest first.

post.summary: Puts an earlier state of a board back, as a new revision.

get.summary: Who can see a project, a list or a page.
Lists workflow steps waiting for a decision.
Lists workflow definitions.

post.summary: Creates a workflow definition.

put.summary: Changes a workflow definition.

delete.summary: Deletes a workflow definition.

patch.summary: Switches a workflow definition on or off.

post.summary: Shows what a workflow would do, without doing it.

get.summary: Lists workflow runs.

post.summary: Starts a workflow run.

get.summary: Reads a workflow run and its steps.

post.summary: Undoes a step.
Approves or rejects a step.
Hands a step's decision to someone else.
Resumes a step.
Retries a step.
Skips a step.

get.summary: The step types a workflow can use.

post.summary: Starts a tracker timer on a task, for the desktop tracker. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. The caller can only start a timer for themselves; a `userId` naming someone else answers 403. Only users marked as tracker users may start one, else it answers `isPermissionDenied`. Reads `description`, `projectId` and `taskId` from the body, all required, plus `considerActionTime` (boolean) and `actionTime` (a Unix time in seconds) to set the start time. A start in an approved, locked period is refused. Answers with `statusText`: the id of the new time entry.

Stores a tracker screenshot on a running timer and moves its end time forward. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `file`, `path`, `companyId`, `timeSheetId`, `key`, `imageName`, `prevscreenShot`, `screenShotTime`, `memoName` and `strokes` (a JSON string) from a form upload; all are required. `companyId` must match the company header, `timeSheetId` must be a timer of the caller that is still running, and `path` must lie in that timer's own capture folder, or it answers 403 (a path already stored answers 409). The image is the uploaded file. Answers with `statusText` `Data Update Succesfully`.

Stores a tracker screenshot on a running timer and moves its end time forward, for the desktop tracker. Any signed-in member of the workspace may call it. Reads `file`, `path`, `companyId`, `timeSheetId`, `key`, `imageName`, `prevscreenShot`, `screenShotTime`, `memoName` and `strokes` (a JSON string) from a form upload; all are required. `companyId` must match the company header, `timeSheetId` must be a timer of the caller that is still running, and `path` must lie in that timer's own capture folder, or it answers 403 (a path already stored answers 409). The image is the uploaded file. Only tracker users may use it, else it answers `isPermissionDenied`. It also reads `considerActionTime` and `actionTime` (seconds) to set the end time. Answers with `statusText` `Data Update Succesfully`.

companyId.name: companyid
companyId.description: The workspace the request is for.
